findings.title: Same NPE remains in the paged/search subgroup methods
findings.body: The fix only guards getSubGroupsCount(). getSubGroupsStream(String, Integer, Integer) (line 256), getSubGroupsStream(Integer, Integer) (line 262) and getSubGroupsStream(String, Boolean, Integer, Integer) (line 268) still call modelSupplier.get().getSubGroupsStream(...) directly. When the group was deleted concurrently, LazyModel returns null and these throw the same NullPointerException the PR is meant to fix. They should null-check the supplier result and return Stream.empty() (or equivalent) like the count method does. Similarly, getAttributes/getFirstAttribute/getAttributeStream (lines 149, 155, 163) pass modelSupplier into CachedGroup.getAttributes, which dereferences the supplier on a cache miss, so a concurrent deletion can still NPE there.

findings.title: Reader thread is never joined, so the test can pass without checking anything
findings.body: The reader thread is started and then deletedAll is set immediately after the deletes, and the assertion on caughtExceptions runs right away. The reader thread is not joined, so it may never have executed a single read, or may still be running and adding exceptions after the assertion has already been evaluated. The check is therefore racy and can pass vacuously. The test should join the reader thread (after setting the flag) before asserting, and ideally assert that at least one read happened.

findings.title: Busy-looping reader thread hammers the server and the failure path is swallowed
findings.body: The reader loops with no pause, issuing a full brief group query as fast as possible for the whole delete phase, which adds unnecessary load and can slow or destabilise the test. Exceptions are only collected into a list that is never inspected until the race is over, and the thread is not managed by the test framework, so an uncaught Error in the thread would be silently lost. Also the group list is never cleaned up on failure. Consider a bounded loop or executor with futures.
